[hrcw] Task 3: Silica adequacy concern – P2 mask specified but no explicit fit-test schedule or filter change frequency defined in controls; 'each shift' mentioned in PPE but not operationalised in monitoring critical control.

[hrcw] Task 6: Hazmat adequacy gap – organic vapour cartridge listed in PPE but not in dominant control logic or monitoring critical control; no cure-time verification before water test in controls section despite hold point mandate.
[ccvs] Task 6: monitoring.critical_control references 'Dust extraction' but dominant hazard is fall/slip—control misaligned to wrong family.
[architecture] Task 3 (Remove membrane) marked hrcw: false but hrcw_category: cl.2 — contradictory classification
[architecture] Task 4 (Investigate cracks) marked hrcw: false but hrcw_category: cl.2 — contradictory classification
[architecture] Task 5 (Repair substrate) marked hrcw: false but hrcw_category: cl.2 — contradictory classification
[architecture] Task 6 (Waterproofing membrane) marked hrcw: false but hrcw_category: cl.2 — contradictory classification
[architecture] Task 7 (Reinstate screed/tiles) marked hrcw: false but hrcw_category: cl.2 — contradictory classification
[architecture] Task 8 (Final inspection) marked hrcw: false but hrcw_category: cl.2 — contradictory classification
[architecture] Task 9 (Dismantle scaffold) marked hrcw: false but hrcw_category: cl.2 — contradictory classification
[architecture] Task 3 admin section incomplete — responsibility fields show truncated text 'Perform Remove existing...'
[architecture] Task 4 admin section shows Leo and Associates holds point but no pre-task structural engineer approval control documented
[architecture] Framework vs work-package: Tasks 2, 3, 6, 7, 9 reuse identical WAH-H6/SIL-H6/CHM-H6 codes across different trades — potential framework misuse
[architecture] Task 1 (Site establishment) precedes scaffold erection but does not explicitly prohibit plant movement until induction complete — latent condition risk
[architecture] Tasks 3–8 all assume scaffold operational but no explicit sequential dependency lock after Task 2 handover
[architecture] Task 5 (Repairs) and Task 6 (Membrane) both depend on Leo and Associates sign-off but Leo approval task sequenced at Task 4 only
[architecture] Document control: No version lock, no approval dates, all marked approved: false and version 1.0 — release status unclear
[architecture] Task 7 PPE section lists high-visibility vest twice (lines differ: 'vest' vs 'High-visibility vest')
[architecture] Task 8 and 9 both reference closed/barricaded balconies but final inspection scope does not confirm occupant re-access criteria
[architecture] No task explicitly addresses latent defect discovery post-membrane cure (e.g. delamination, peel-back) — remediation scope undefined

[hrcw] Task 3: HRCW undercall – dominant hazard is 'struck by falling debris' (consequence 3) but marked hrcw=false. Should be cl.2 HRCW given 4m+ height, occupied building below, and silica exposure.

[hrcw] Task 3: Dominant hazard logic mismatch – 'struck by falling tiles' selected but silica inhalation listed first and has equivalent or higher risk given respiratory harm severity; dominant hazard should be silica or co-dominant.
[hrcw] Task 5: Dominant hazard undercall – 'slip on wet material' is lower consequence than fall-from-height risk during grind/prep; dominant should be fall or slip + fall combination at 4m+.

[hrcw] Task 6: Dominant hazard overcall – 'fall during water-test' is lower likelihood than fume inhalation during prime/membrane application; dominant hazard logic suggests fume should be primary with fall secondary.

[hrcw] Task 7: HRCW undercall – silica dust during tile cutting + fall from height at 4m+ during wet screed work; marked hrcw=false but dominant hazard is fall-from-height (cl.2 HRCW category confirmed in field). Inconsistent.

[hrcw] Task 9: Dominant hazard logic sound but risk scoring inconsistent – pre-score likelihood=3, consequence=3 (High 9) but post-score likelihood=2, consequence=3 (Medium 6) assumes harness reduces likelihood only, not consequence; consequence of fall from 4m remains 3.
[hrcw] Task 1: No HRCW; correct – site establishment is SYS-M3, no height work, dominant hazard is vehicle strike with medium pre-risk and low post-risk via barriers/comms. Logic sound.
[ccvs] Task 3 (Remove membrane): CCVS code SIL-H6 assigned but dominant hazard is 'Struck by falling tiles' (WAH). Should be WAH-H6.
[ccvs] Task 5 (Repair substrate): CCVS code SIL-H6 assigned but dominant hazard is 'Slip on wet material at height' (WAH). Should be WAH-H6.
[ccvs] Task 6 (Apply membrane): CCVS code CHM-H6 assigned but dominant hazard is 'Fall during water-test' (WAH). Should be WAH-H6.
[ccvs] Task 4 (Investigate cracks): CCVS code SYS-M3 misaligned; dominant hazard 'Fall from height' requires WAH-H6 code.
[ccvs] Task 8 (Final inspection): CCVS code SYS-M3 misaligned; dominant hazard 'Fall from height' requires WAH-H6 code.
[ccvs] All 9 tasks show wah_applicable=true but only tasks 2,3,5,6,7,9 correctly coded WAH. Tasks 1,4,8 coded non-WAH despite height/fall hazards.
[ccvs] Task 3: Evidence field states 'debris netting visual inspection record (daily)' but monitoring section lacks specific debris netting checklist.
[ccvs] Task 5: monitoring.evidence names 'matting installed or residue removed' but no daily inspection checklist row exists in admin.
[ccvs] Task 7: monitoring.responsibility SUP/WKR rows reference 'module weights' (EWP language) not scaffold loads.
[ccvs] Task 9: monitoring.evidence requires 'daily photo of harness setup' but no photo archiving procedure documented in admin.

[credibility] Task 1: Unsupported admin control — 'owners corporation special resolution' and 'strata by-law compliance' embedded in governance checklist without evidence they apply to occupied remedial works scope.
[credibility] Task 2: Scaffold erection permit listed as control, not prerequisite — permit is framework gate, not live task step.

[credibility] Task 3: Silica HRCW (SIL-H6) coherent with task content and dust extraction evidence; dominant hazard (falling debris) correctly sequenced. CCVS evidence checks wet suppression + RPE fit — appropriate.
[credibility] Task 4: CCVS code SYS-M3 assigned to crack inspection (fall-from-height dominant hazard) — should be WAH-specific code. Mismatch between dominant hazard and monitoring framework.
[credibility] Task 5: Slip hazard controls present but HRCW set to false despite 4m+ work and fall risk scored High(6). Inconsistent with task content.
[credibility] Task 6: Membrane cure-time hold point references 'manufacturer data sheet' but no SDS attachment or baseline cure schedule provided — control is performative, not evidenced.
[credibility] Task 7: Tile cutting relocated to ground level (good), but admin checklist includes unsupported 'verify scaffolding licence class' — worker licence class not a control for this phase.

[credibility] Task 8: Final inspection task assigns SYS-M3 (system/management) to fall-from-height dominant hazard at 4m+ — code mismatch. Edge protection removed mid-task per scope but hold point requires it.

[credibility] Task 9: Dismantling sequence correct per scaffold method, but 'anemometer on site hourly checks' is granular detail not typical live control. Responsibilty fields copy-pasted from Task 2 (scaffold erection) — wrong role assignment.

[credibility] Cross-task: 'Close and barricaded balconies directly below' repeated in 6 tasks but never operationalised — no resident lock protocol, no access control evidence tied to balcony closure.
[credibility] Cross-task: Leo and Associates inspection (Tasks 4, 8) referenced as hold point but no contact, scope of inspection, or approval authority documented.
[credibility] Cross-task: Occupant notification requirements scatter across 8 tasks with no centralised communication log template or escalation threshold — administrative burden untracked.

[credibility] Task 11: ccvs_code WAH-H6 assigned but monitoring section empty (critical_control blank) and content is general site cleanup, not fall prevention.
[credibility] Task 8 (Lay tiles): 'Dust extraction running' listed as critical control but task is tile laying with water cutting only—silica dust hazard not dominant for this phase.
[architecture] Sequence 4 (crack inspection) positioned before sequence 3 (removal) — defect assessment must follow substrate exposure, not precede it.

[architecture] Sequence 5 (crack repair) and sequence 6 (membrane) violate mandatory waterproofing workflow — repair must cure fully before membrane application; no hold point enforces cure verification.
[architecture] Sequence 7 (screed/tile bed) scheduled before membrane curing period documented — latent water ingress risk if membrane not fully cured.
[architecture] Task 1 (site setup) references 'balcony closure' but sequence 2 (scaffold erection) precedes balcony access control — cart before horse.
[architecture] Sequence 8 (final tiling) and 9 (inspection) lack integration — inspection may trigger rework, but tile adhesive cure time not blocked.
[architecture] Sequence 11 task lists 'wah_applicable: true' but task is ground-level demobilisation — incorrect HRCW classification.
[architecture] No latent condition packaging — tasks 4, 5, 6 assume slab condition known, but no pre-work survey gate before sequence 1.
[architecture] Document control absent — 11 tasks all 'approved: false' and 'source: ai-generated' with no revision freeze or sign-off framework.
[architecture] Task 3 (removal) and task 4 (inspection) both trigger environmental hazards but no air quality baseline or post-removal validation hold point.
[architecture] Sequence 10 (scaffold dismantle) references 'certifier release' but task 2 (erect) does not mandate certifier appointment — missing initial control.
[hrcw] Task 11 (demobilisation): HRCW=false but wah_applicable=true - contradictory; demobilisation is non-elevated, should be HRCW=false, wah_applicable=false
[hrcw] Task 11: ccvs_code='WAH-H6' assigned to non-HRCW ground task - incorrect; should be SYS-M3 or similar
[hrcw] Task 7 (screed): dominant_hazard='Fall from height' but silica/cement dust inhalation is equal/dominant risk - undercall of chemical/respiratory hazard
[hrcw] Task 3 (membrane removal): silica dominant hazard correctly identified but Task 7 screed dust hazard downplayed despite wet cement/additives mixing
[hrcw] Task 5 (crack repair): CCVS code='SIL-H6' correct for silica, but admin requires EPA Category 31 air emissions licence - hazmat adequacy weak (no VOC or fume monitoring specified)

[hrcw] Task 6 (membrane application): dominant_hazard='toxic chemical fumes' correctly identified; CCVS='CHM-H6' appropriate; isocyanate sensitisation briefing required but no baseline health surveillance or re-exposure protocol documented
[hrcw] Task 3, 5, 6: No mention of material safety data or product-specific hazard verification before site delivery - assumes SDS review only on-site
[hrcw] Task 2 (scaffold erection): HRCW_category='cl.2' correct for <4m; wah_applicable=true appropriate; no mention of class 1 vs 2 determination or alternative EWP assessment
[hrcw] Task 8 (tiling): dominant_hazard='trip hazard' appropriate; silica dust from tile cutting addressed but wet-cut control assumes water supply available on scaffold - no backup method
[hrcw] Tasks 3,5,6,7: Repetitive CCVS code 'SIL-H6' applied to different hazard types (silica, cement, chemicals) - code reuse may mask task-specific control family mismatch
[hrcw] Task 1 (site setup): HRCW=false correct; adequately scoped for interface management; occupied building controls comprehensive
[hrcw] Task 4 (crack documentation): wah_applicable=true but no actual work-at-height risk beyond platform access; classification may be overcall if observation-only
[ccvs] Task 11 (Site demobilisation): CCVS code WAH-H6 assigned but wah_applicable=false and hrcw=false. Non-WAH task misaligned to WAH code.
[ccvs] Task 4 (Check slab): CCVS code SYS-M3 but dominant_hazard is fall-from-height (WAH). Should map to WAH-H6.
[ccvs] Task 1 (Site setup): CCVS code SYS-M3 correct but wah_applicable=false despite occupied building fall hazards in shared access. Consider WAH applicability.

[ccvs] Task 7 (Install screed): Evidence field monitoring states 'Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle' but task is screed application, not grinding. Misaligned evidence descriptor.
[ccvs] Task 8 (Lay tiles): Evidence field states same grinding/dust extraction language as Task 7 despite no grinding in screed/tile laying scope. Copy-paste error.
[ccvs] Task 11 (Site demobilisation): monitoring.critical_control field is empty string. monitoring.who_checks and monitoring.what_to_look_for are duplicate fields; should consolidate.
[ccvs] Task 11: wah_applicable=true contradicts hrcw=false. High-risk fall tasks during scaffold dismantling but WAH flag inconsistent with demobilisation hazard profile.
[ccvs] Tasks 3, 5, 6: SIL-H6 or CHM-H6 codes dominate but no cross-reference to silica or chemical CCVS family definitions provided. Assume alignment but unverified.
[ccvs] Task 9 (Inspection): CCVS code SYS-M3 assigned but hazards centre on fall-from-height during final work. WAH-H6 likely more appropriate.
[ccvs] Missing N/A rows: No indication which tasks were screened out as N/A or why certain CCVS codes were selected over alternatives.
[credibility] Task 11 (Site demobilisation): wah_applicable marked TRUE but no working-at-heights hazards present—demobilisation is ground-level removal work only.
[credibility] Task 4 (Check slab): HRCW cl.2 applied but dominant hazard is 'slip on slab'—this is routine inspection, not elevated high-risk work. Scaling misaligned.
[credibility] Task 1 (Site setup): 'Scaffold handover certificate' listed as live control in hold point but scaffold erection is separate task 2. Framework control embedded in operational task.
[credibility] Task 3 (Remove membrane): 'asbestos-suspect material separately' mentioned as control but source scope confirms 'latent only'—no active asbestos management justified.
[credibility] Task 5 (Repair cracks): 'EPA air emissions licence Category 31' required in admin but no coating/sealing system described in task scope—unsupported administrative burden.
[credibility] Task 6 (Apply membrane): Monitoring requires 'worker respiratory check every 15 minutes' but no competency or medical clearance procedure defined—CCVS H6 control incomplete.

[credibility] Multiple tasks (3, 5, 6, 8): 'Close and barricade balconies directly below' repeated as admin requirement—residents responsibility not contractor; occupant dependency creates unmanaged control.
[credibility] Task 2 (Scaffold erection): RIIOHS204E competency required but no RIIOHS204D (supervisor) or RIIOHS205C (senior) alternative stated—unnecessarily rigid.
[credibility] Task 1: 'Residents responsible for clearing personal items...area excluded if not cleared'—contractual liability assigned without hold point enforcement or exclusion protocol.
